s: One SELECT per test, combined with UNION ALL into (TestName, FailingRows).
Make each test return rows that fail, so zero means pass and the number is directly actionable.
Run it after every load; in Power BI, a model on top of this query gives a data quality page.

code.title: Data quality suite
src: SELECT 'duplicate line keys' AS TestName, COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(OrderID, '|', "LineNo")) AS FailingRows FROM order_lines
UNION ALL SELECT 'orphan lines', COUNT(*) FROM order_lines AS l WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.OrderID = l.OrderID)
UNION ALL SELECT 'orphan returns', COUNT(*) FROM returns AS r WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.OrderID = r.OrderID)
UNION ALL SELECT 'non-positive quantity', COUNT(*) FROM order_lines WHERE Qty IS NULL OR Qty <= 0
UNION ALL SELECT 'returned more than sold', COUNT(*) FROM returns AS r
WHERE r.Qty > (SELECT MAX(l.Qty) FROM order_lines AS l WHERE l.OrderID = r.OrderID AND l."LineNo" = r."LineNo")
UNION ALL SELECT 'ship before order', COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE ShipDate IS NOT NULL AND ShipDate < OrderDate
UNION ALL SELECT 'EUR month without rate', COUNT(*) FROM orders AS o
WHERE o.Currency = 'EUR' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fx_rates AS f WHERE f.Month = SUBSTRING(CAST(o.OrderDate AS VARCHAR(10)), 1, 7))
UNION ALL SELECT 'test customer orders', COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE CustomerID = 'C19999';

qa-data-0.check: Duplicates {{sql_dup_rows|int}} and test-customer orders {{qa_test_customer_orders|int}} fail; everything else is 0.
qa-data-0.note: Decide per test whether a failure blocks the load (duplicates) or is a known, handled condition (the test customer, filtered out in the view).

s: Count after Remove Top Rows (−1 header), Remove Bottom Rows (−1 TOTAL) and Remove Duplicates (−1).
Assert source = kept + removed at each step; in Power Query add a step that errors if the counts don't match, so the refresh fails loudly.
Better: run the same reconciliation in the source view, before Power BI.
Block: anything that makes numbers wrong silently (duplicate fact keys, totals that don't reconcile).
Warn and continue: problems with a safe treatment that stays visible (missing members → Unknown; a large row-count drop, which might be real, e.g. a holiday).
Report weekly: quality trends that don't change today's numbers (optional-column nulls, refresh duration creeping up).
Write the policy down; revisit after each incident.
qa-data-2.check: Any split is fine if each choice is tied to business impact and the blocking set is small enough that people don't learn to ignore it.
